surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMA and surface hydroxyl groups followed by water pulse to regenerate OH sites.
evidence: In contrast, TMA reacts with H/Si (100) at 300 °C. An initial TMA exposure [Fig. 1 (c),2 3×10^5 L] predominantly forms Si–CH3 (1266 cm^-1) at Si defect sites, and higher TMA exposures [Fig. 1 (d) 5 3×10^7 L] give rise to Al–CH3 species (1217 cm^-1). 10 While oxidized TMA, probably due to gas impurities, leads to the formation of interfacial Si–O–Al bond arrangements (800 and 1000–1100 cm^-1),10,18 inadvertent SiO2 formation is limited to less than 0.25 Å. Once the H/Si (100) surface has been functionalized by TMA, a water pulse (e) replaces Al-bonded CH3 (but not Si-bonded CH3) by OD and gives rise to subsurface SiO2. In the subsequent cycles (f), amorphous Al2O3 is grown, while additional subsurface Si oxidation is catalyzed by interfacial aluminum.10
